predecessors.name: Marinid Sultanate
predecessors.text: Ceuta, taken 'from the Marinid Sultanate' on 21 August 1415

successors.name: Morocco
successors.text: Mazagan (El Jadida), the last Portuguese foothold, evacuated 10 March 1769

ledger.x: 1505: Portugal founds Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue at Agadir.
September 1541: Agadir falls to the Saadis.
October 1541: the Portuguese evacuate Safi and Azemmour.
1550: the Portuguese leave Ksar es-Seghir and Asilah.
10 March 1769: Portugal evacuates Mazagan, its last foothold in Morocco.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Ceuta
wars.outcome: Portugal took Ceuta on 21 August 1415 from the Marinid Sultanate; the Marinid sultan Abu Said Uthman III sent no aid.

wars.name: Marinid siege of Ceuta
wars.outcome: 'Abu Said Uthman III laid siege to Ceuta with the help of the Nasrid Emir of Granada Muhammad VIII'; the Portuguese repulsed it.

wars.name: Portuguese expansion in Morocco
wars.outcome: Ksar es-Seghir in 1458, Arzila and Tangier in 1471, Safi from 1488, Agadir 1505-06, Azemmour 1513, Mazagan 1514-17, Casablanca and Mehdya 1515; the conflicts page lists the Wattasid Sultanate as a belligerent from 1472 to 1554.

wars.name: Fall of Agadir and the Saadi campaign of 1541
wars.outcome: Muhammad al-Shaykh besieged Santa Cruz do Cabo de Gue for six months (March-September 1541); the Portuguese then evacuated Safi and Azemmour in October.

wars.name: Battle of Alcacer Quibir (Ksar el-Kebir)
wars.outcome: Fought 'on 4 August 1578'; no territorial change is on the pages opened for Portuguese Morocco.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War and Ceuta
wars.outcome: Ceuta stayed with Spain in 1640 and was acknowledged Spanish in the Treaty of Lisbon (1668).

wars.name: Moroccan reconquest of Mazagan
wars.outcome: The Portuguese evacuated Mazagan on 10 March 1769; a Peace and Friendship Agreement followed in 1774.

certainty.note: Fortified towns held by garrisons: the walls are the territory; no hinterland frontier exists on the pages, and the 25 km circles are about the grid minimum for a coastal town.

sources.title: European enclaves in North Africa before 1830
